esde.label: ES-DE
esde.note: System folders use the ES-DE names.

knulli.label: Knulli
knulli.note: Card root is the SHARE partition (/userdata). Folder names are case-sensitive and use Batocera system names; Knulli only scans subfolders of roms/. Systems with knulli = null have no Knulli system.

onion.label: Onion
onion.note: Miyoo Mini family (SigmaStar SSD202D) running Onion. Card root is the FAT32 SD card; Onion creates missing Roms/ folders on first install. Folder names are case sensitive, differ from the stock Miyoo card, and are not ES-DE or Batocera names. Subfolders work only one level deep (e.g. Roms/GB/Hacks). The discs of multi-disc games go in a hidden .multi-disc subfolder with the .m3u beside it, so the list shows each game once. BIOS files go in the root BIOS/ folder unless a system says otherwise. Systems with onion = null have no verified Onion folder. Source: https://onionui.github.io/docs/emulators/folders

allium.label: Allium
allium.note: Miyoo Mini family (SigmaStar SSD202D) running Allium, which uses the Onion card layout and matches systems by file extension first, so the folders are the same as Onion's. Allium reads a gamelist.xml (path, name, image, rating, releasedate, developer, publisher, genre) in each ROM folder and finds box art in Imgs/. Sources: https://github.com/goweiwen/Allium/wiki/2.-Add-your-Games!, https://github.com/goweiwen/Allium

muos.label: muOS
muos.note: MustardOS on Anbernic H700 handhelds (and the RG Vita Pro). Card root is the games partition (exFAT or FAT32). muOS matches folder names to systems ignoring case, spaces, hyphens and underscores, so the names here are the Knulli ones where muOS knows them. Systems with muos = null have no muOS system. Source: https://muos.dev/systems/cores

slot.label: Slot
slot.note: slot, a Game Boy-centric frontend (GB, GBC and GBA only) for the Anbernic RG SP and other H700 handhelds. Card root is the SD card slot runs from. ROMs must be unzipped and sit directly in their system folder, so a sync extracts archives and ignores subfolders. Source: https://slot-cfw.fyi

emudeck.label: EmuDeck
emudeck.note: EmuDeck on the Steam Deck and Steam Machine (SteamOS). Card root holds Emulation/; emulators install to the internal SSD. System folders use the ES-DE names, except Wii U, Xbox 360 and Model 2, which keep their ROMs in a roms/ subfolder. BIOS files go in Emulation/bios, with subfolders only where an emulator expects one. Source: https://emudeck.github.io/cheat-sheet/
